content:
Using Signal and need to switch between multiple devices? The encrypted messaging service is making it easier for users to use the app across different iPhones and other devices.

Signal users can now link another iPhone to their existing Signal account, rather than limiting secondary mobile devices to iPads only.

The company announced today: "We're expanding linked device support on iOS, letting you link an iPhone to your Signal account, and our support for iPad will continue." The announcement also included new Android linking support.

When linking an additional iPhone, users can choose whether to transfer their full message history, along with media files stored in the past 45 days.

Signal says the transfer process uses fully end-to-end encryption and uses the same "link-and-sync" technology as iPad and desktop devices (including the Mac Signal app).

This expanded support is especially useful for users who need to use both personal and work iPhones at the same time, or who test on multiple devices.

The move also brings Signal's multi-device experience closer to Apple's Messages ecosystem, where conversations sync between iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Signal for iOS version 8.22 is rolling out now on the App Store. Signal recently launched a username feature that lets users connect without sharing a phone number.
